summary: The Paleobiology Database holds the core data openly (georeferenced, dated marine occurrences with formation and member names, plus per-species first and last appearance ages) and Macrostrat links PBDB collections to formation units. What no source gives is the order of occurrences inside a single formation, so 'first appearance partway through a formation' can only be approximated from formation membership and age bounds.
next_step: Pull Neogene marine bivalve and gastropod occurrences with formation and age bounds, define local first occurrence per formation, and compare with the oldest occurrence elsewhere; pre-register how age-bin overlap is treated.
obstacles_confirmed: Bed-level stratigraphic position within a formation is not in PBDB (only formation, member and age bounds were seen in the returned fields).
A sampled Bivalvia species record (Paradoxia timorensis) has noc 1, an example of single-occurrence taxa; the share of such species was not measured.
